title: स्नातक तहको नेपाली भाषा कक्षामा सिकाइ सहजीकरणको उपयोग {The Use of Learning Naturalization in the Nepali Education Class of Bachelor}
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेख सिकाइ सहजीकरणका क्षेत्रमा केन्द्रित छ । यस लेखको उद्देश्य त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालयअन्तर्गत स्नातक तहको नेपाली भाषा कक्षामा सिकाइ सहजीकरणको उपयोगको अवस्थाका बारेमा शिक्षकहरूको धारणा पहिल्याउनु रहेको छ । यो अनुसन्धान गुणात्मक ढाँचा, व्याख्यावादी दर्शन, घटना अनुभव पद्धति र रचनावादी (निर्माणवादी) सिद्धान्तमा आधारित छ । यसका लागि पोखरा महानगरपालिकाका स्नातक तहमा अध्यापन गर्ने शिक्षकलाई सूचकका रूपमा लिई अन्तर्वार्ता उपकरणका माध्यमबाट उनीहरूका सिकाइ सहजीकरणसँग सम्बन्धित जीवन्त अनुभव सङ्कलन गरिएको छ । प्राप्त तथ्याङ्कलाई अभिलेखन गर्ने, सङ्केतन गर्ने र आशय (थिम) बनाई प्रस्तुतीकरणका साथ छलफल गरी निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ । अनुसन्धानको प्राप्तितर्फ दृष्टि दिँदा उक्त तहका नेपाली भाषा विषयका विद्यार्थीहरू सिकाइमा नियमित, सक्रिय र सहभागी भएको पाइन्छ । सिकाइ सहजीकरणमा स्तरअनुसारका विधि, सामग्री, सूचना र प्रविधि तथा कक्षा व्यवस्थापन भएको पाइन्छ । सिकारुलाई सिद्धान्त र व्यवहारबिच समन्वय गराई आत्मप्रतिविम्बन र बहुबौद्धिकताको उपयोगका साथ ज्ञान हस्तान्तरण गर्ने नभई उनीहरूमा ज्ञानको निर्माण गर्ने अवसर दिनुपर्छ भन्ने शिक्षकको अभिमत देखिन्छ । सहयोगात्मक सिकाइ, सिर्जनात्मक र परियोजना कार्य तथा विद्यार्थीलाई नै समस्याको समाधान गर्न उत्प्रेरित गर्ने र आवश्यक पृष्ठपोषण दिने गर्नाले सिकारुमा अपनत्वको भावनाको विकास भई सिकाइमा स्थायी परिवर्तन आउने धारणा सम्बन्धित शिक्षकहरूको छ । अतः स्नातक तहको नेपाली भाषा कक्षामा सिकाइ सहजीकरणको उपयोग गर्दा यस्ता पक्षहरूमा ध्यान दिनु आवश्यक देखिन्छ । सिकाइ सहजीकरणको उपयोगका विषयमा रुचि राख्ने अध्येताका लागि प्रस्तुत लेखले सहयोग पु¥याउने अपेक्षा राखिएको छ।
american_english: The present article is centered on the field of learning facilitation. The objective of this article is to ascertain teachers' perceptions regarding the condition of the use of learning facilitation in Nepali language classes at the bachelor's level under Tribhuvan University. This research is based on a qualitative design, interpretivist philosophy, phenomenological method, and constructivist (constructionist) theory. For this, teachers teaching at the bachelor's level in Pokhara Metropolitan City were taken as informants, and their lived experiences related to learning facilitation were collected through the interview instrument. The obtained data were recorded, coded, and made into themes (theme); after presenting them and holding a discussion, a conclusion was drawn. Looking at the findings of the research, students of the Nepali language subject at that level are found to be regular, active, and participatory in learning. Learning facilitation is found to involve level-appropriate methods, materials, information and technology, and classroom management. The teachers' view appears to be that, coordinating theory and practice and using self-reflection and multiple intelligences, learners should be given the opportunity to construct knowledge within themselves rather than to transfer knowledge to them. The concerned teachers hold the view that cooperative learning, creative and project work, motivating students themselves to solve problems, and giving necessary feedback develop a sense of ownership in learners and bring about lasting change in learning. Therefore, it appears necessary to pay attention to these aspects when using learning facilitation in the Nepali language class at the bachelor's level. It is hoped that this article will assist researchers interested in the use of learning facilitation.

australian_english: This article centres on the field of learning facilitation. Its objective is to work out teachers' perceptions of the state of the use of learning facilitation in Nepali language classes at bachelor's level under Tribhuvan University. The research is grounded in a qualitative design, interpretivist philosophy, phenomenological method and constructivist (constructionist) theory. To do this, teachers teaching at bachelor's level in Pokhara Metropolitan City were used as informants, and their lived experiences around learning facilitation were collected through the interview instrument. The data gathered were recorded, coded and turned into themes (theme), and after being presented and discussed, conclusions were drawn. Looking at what the research turned up, Nepali language students at that level come across as regular, active and participatory in their learning. Learning facilitation is found to involve level-appropriate methods, materials, information and technology, and classroom management. Teachers appear to hold the view that, by bringing theory and practice together and drawing on self-reflection and multiple intelligences, learners should be given the chance to construct knowledge in themselves rather than have knowledge transferred to them. The teachers concerned believe that collaborative learning, creative and project work, and motivating students to solve problems themselves with the necessary feedback all build a sense of ownership in learners and bring lasting change to their learning. It is therefore clear that these aspects need to be kept in mind when using learning facilitation in the Nepali language class at bachelor's level. This article is expected to help researchers with an interest in the use of learning facilitation.
informal_english: So this article is all about the learning facilitation space. The whole aim is to suss out what teachers reckon about how learning facilitation's actually being used in Nepali-language bachelor's classes under Tribhuvan University. The study's based on a qualitative design, interpretivist philosophy, phenomenology and constructivist (constructionist) theory. To do that, bachelor-level teachers at Pokhara Metropolitan City were used as informants, and their lived experiences around learning facilitation were gathered through interviews. The data was recorded, coded and turned into themes, then presented, discussed, and conclusions were drawn. Looking at what came out of it, Nepali-language students at that level are turning up regularly, staying active and getting involved in their learning. Learning facilitation is using methods, materials, info and tech matched to level, plus decent class management. The teachers reckon learners shouldn't just have knowledge handed down to them — they should get the chance to build it themselves, linking theory up with practice, with self-reflection and multiple intelligences thrown in. Co-operative learning, creative and project work, getting the students to crack their own problems and giving them the feedback they need builds a sense of ownership in learners and brings lasting change to their learning — that's what the teachers reckon, anyway. So, bottom line: if you're going to use learning facilitation in the Nepali bachelor's class, you've got to keep these things in mind. Hopefully this article helps out anyone keen on using learning facilitation.
